What Changed Since CRAN 1.6.1

Source: vignettes/articles/changes-since-cran.Rmd
changes-since-cran.Rmd

CRAN serves RMediation 1.6.1. Releases 1.7.0 to 1.11.1 are on GitHub only (see Status and Roadmap and Reporting RMediation in a Paper for how to install a tag). This page lists what can change a number you already have or break code you already wrote. The News page has every change by version; this page does not repeat the bug fixes that only affect rare inputs.

1. Results that changed

Re-run anything you computed with 1.6.1 if it falls under one of these.

Version What changed Who is affected
1.7.0 pprodnormal3() now integrates with Gauss-Legendre quadrature by default (method = "gauss"). The earlier adaptive integrator (method = "hcubature", still available) returned wrong values on ill-conditioned covariance, silently. Anyone using pprodnormal3(), ProductNormal3, or ci() on three-factor products, above all with highly correlated estimates. Well-conditioned input agrees to about 1e-6.
1.8.0 The CDF of the product of two normals is exact at |rho| = 1, and no longer collapses at large standardized means (pprodnormal(), qprodnormal(), medci()). |rho| = 1, or paths with a large estimate relative to its standard error.
1.8.0 Point masses use the right-continuous CDF: pprodnormal3() returned 0.5 at q == 0 for a product identically zero; it now returns 1. Zero-variance inputs.
1.8.0 medci(type = "mc") reports MC.Error as SE / sqrt(n.mc); it was SE / n.mc. Intervals and estimates did not change. Anyone reading MC.Error.
1.9.0 ci(type = "asymp") names its interval by its confidence level (95% CI at the default). It was 97.5% CI. The interval itself was always correct. Code that indexes the result by the old name.
1.9.0 dprodnormal() and dprodnormal3() no longer return 0, NA or a silently low density when a mean is very large relative to its standard error. Large mu / se.

Three of these you can see directly:

# 1.6.1 returned about 8e-7 here; the correct value is about 0.507
pprodnormal(400, mu.x = 20, mu.y = 20, se.x = 1, se.y = 1)
#> [1] 0.5070403

# a product identically equal to 0 is at or below 0 with probability 1
pprodnormal3(0, mean = c(0, 0, 0), cov = matrix(0, 3, 3))
#> [1] 1

# the interval is labeled by its confidence level
names(ci(c(a = 0.5, b = 0.6), diag(c(0.08, 0.04)^2), ~ a * b, type = "asymp"))
#> [1] "95% CI"   "Estimate" "SE"

2. Code that may stop working

  • medci_prototype() is removed (1.8.0). It shipped in 1.6.1 as an exported prototype that nothing in the package called. Use medci(), or ci() on a ProductNormal; they return the same intervals.
  • pprodnormal3() rejects an invalid covariance (1.8.0): one that is not finite and positive semidefinite, including negative variances at very different scales. It used to clamp negative variances to zero.
  • mbco() is stricter (1.8.0). It checks the constraints of h0 and h1 at the fitted solution and signals classed conditions (RMediation_constraint_violation, RMediation_constraint_not_enforced, RMediation_h0_refit_failed and others; the Quick Reference lists them). type = "parametric" now checks every bootstrap replicate like type = "semi" does, and stops with RMediation_bootstrap_infeasible when it cannot repair one, where it used to let a bad replicate into the null distribution. Equal-df and reversed model pairs are rejected.
  • Defined parameters in ci(<lavaan>) used to stop the whole call on a := that uses another :=, and on a product of three or more coefficients under most type values. They now return a result (1.10.0); see below.

3. New since 1.6.1

Version Addition
1.8.0 dprodnormal() and dprodnormal3(), the exact densities of the product of two and three normals
1.8.0 pprodnormal() and qprodnormal() accept vectors
1.8.0 mbco_product_null(): an exact test of a*b = 0 that cannot land on the wrong branch
1.8.0 ml_omitted_confounder(): sensitivity of two-level 1-1-1 mediation to an omitted confounder
1.8.0 mbco(h0, h1, type = "asymp") on two medfit SEMFit fits (needs medfit 0.8.0 or later)
1.10.0 @provenance on mbco() results: versions, test type, bootstrap size, RNGkind() and run time (the seed is not recorded)
1.10.0 ci(<lavaan>) resolves a := built from other := and handles products of three or more coefficients

The defined-parameter rules in 1.10.0 are easiest to see on a small fit:

set.seed(2)
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(300))
d$m <- 0.5 * d$x + rnorm(300)
d$y <- 0.4 * d$m + 0.2 * d$x + rnorm(300)
fit <- lavaan::sem("m ~ a*x\n y ~ b*m + cp*x\n ab := a*b\n abx := ab*a", d)
res <- suppressWarnings(ci(fit, type = "MC", n.mc = 5000))
names(res)
#> [1] "ab"  "abx"

abx := ab*a is a*b*a, a product that repeats a coefficient. Releases up to 1.10.0 stop on it for every type except "MC"; 1.11.0 gives it a Monte Carlo interval with a warning when you chose another type.

4. New in 1.11.0

See the 1.11.0 entry on the News page.

  • A coefficient repeated inside a product of three or more factors gets a Monte Carlo interval instead of an error.
  • pprodnormal3() accepts a vector of q, like the other distribution functions, and takes lower.tail; with lower.tail = FALSE it integrates the upper tail directly, so far tails are resolved (use a tol well below the probability you want).
  • qprodnormal3() is new: the quantile of the product of three normals, both tails. dist_quantile() on a ProductNormal3 uses the same routine and now returns -Inf and Inf at p = 0 and p = 1.
  • ?ci now documents the p element of the Monte Carlo result (a sign proportion, not a null test).

5. New in 1.11.1

See the 1.11.1 entry on the News page. It fixes bugs only.

  • cdf() on a ProductNormal3 with lower.tail = FALSE integrates the upper tail directly, and dist_quantile() and confint() use the object’s integration method.
  • dist_quantile() on a ProductNormal accepts a vector of probabilities.
  • ci(mu = ..., Sigma = ...) stops with a message saying to pass the estimates by position; ?ci lists the numeric-form arguments.

Which version to cite

Report the tag you ran, not dev: Reporting RMediation in a Paper lists what to record, and the Quick Reference has the one-page summary of functions and result shapes.
